zebralogic.title: Interpret adjacency and ordering clues correctly
zebralogic.principle: When a clue uses terms like 'directly left of', 'directly right of', or similar, enforce that the two houses are adjacent in the specified order.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue mentions direct adjacency or ordering between two attributes.
zebralogic.example: Treating 'directly left of' as a non‑adjacent ordering and placing the houses apart.

zebralogic.title: Interpret distance clues correctly
zebralogic.principle: When a clue says 'N houses between X and Y', enforce that exactly N houses separate X and Y (|pos(X) - pos(Y)| = N+1).
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue specifies a numeric distance between two attributes.
zebralogic.example: Interpreting 'one house between' as the houses being adjacent.

zebralogic.title: Treat 'somewhere left/right of' as inequality
zebralogic.principle: Interpret phrases like 'X is somewhere left of Y' (or right of) as a strict ordering constraint (pos(X) < pos(Y) or >), without requiring adjacency.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue uses 'somewhere left/right of' without the word 'directly'.
zebralogic.example: Treating 'somewhere left of' as adjacency and placing X immediately left of Y.

zebralogic.title: Enforce uniqueness across each attribute category
zebralogic.principle: Each value in a category must appear exactly once across all houses; no two houses may share the same value.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: During assignment, ensure no duplicate values within a category.
zebralogic.example: Assigning the same color to two different houses.

zebralogic.title: Preserve original case of attribute values
zebralogic.principle: When outputting the final grid, copy each attribute value exactly as it appears in the problem statement, preserving capitalization.

zebralogic.title: Bidirectional equivalence for name‑attribute clues
zebralogic.principle: When a clue directly links a specific name to an attribute, enforce both directions (name ↔ attribute).
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue says 'X is the Y' or 'Y belongs to X'.
zebralogic.example: Only enforcing 'Bob is the desert‑smoothie lover' in one direction, allowing Bob to have a different smoothie.

zebralogic.title: Bidirectional equivalence for attribute‑attribute clues
zebralogic.principle: When a clue links two non‑name attributes, enforce both directions (attribute A ↔ attribute B).
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue says 'The cat lover is the person whose mother is Sarah' or similar.
zebralogic.example: Only applying the link one way, leaving the other attribute unconstrained.

zebralogic.title: Apply direct placement constraints
zebralogic.principle: When a clue explicitly places an attribute in a specific house, enforce that placement.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue mentions a house number or position.
zebralogic.example: Ignoring 'The lime smoothie drinker lives in house 2' and allowing lime elsewhere.

zebralogic.title: Output solution JSON with exact schema and no extra text
zebralogic.principle: When finalizing the answer, emit only the JSON object with the required keys and structure, without any explanatory text or stray characters.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: At the very end of the response.
zebralogic.example: Including a narrative before the JSON, causing parsing failure.

zebralogic.title: Disambiguate overlapping attribute categories
zebralogic.principle: When multiple attribute categories contain overlapping values (e.g., 'cat' appears in both Pet and Animal), determine which category a clue refers to and keep each category's values separate; never assign a value from one category to the other.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue mentions a value that exists in more than one category, or when filling the solution grid, ensure each column receives values from its own category.
zebralogic.example: Assigning the pet 'cat' to the Animal column because a clue said 'cat lover', leading to swapped categories.

zebralogic.description: Interpreting 'N houses between' as distance N
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model treats the number in the clue as the total gap rather than the number of houses separating the two positions.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: When a clue says 'N houses between X and Y', enforce that the absolute position difference equals N+1.

zebralogic.description: Ignoring equivalence clues that bind two attributes to the same house
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model fails to propagate bidirectional constraints, treating the link as one‑way.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Whenever a clue links two attributes, enforce both directions so they occupy the same house.

zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model may assign the same value to multiple houses within a category, overlooking the uniqueness constraint.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Track used values per category and prevent duplicates during assignment.

zebralogic.description: Altering attribute values (spelling/casing) instead of copying them verbatim
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model normalizes text or makes typographical changes during generation.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Copy attribute strings exactly as given, preserving case and spelling.

zebralogic.description: Including extra explanatory text or stray characters outside the required JSON solution
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model adds commentary or formatting before/after the JSON, breaking the parser.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Output only the JSON object with the required keys, no surrounding text.

zebralogic.description: Confusing overlapping attribute categories (e.g., swapping values between 'Pet' and 'Animal')
zebralogic.why_it_happens: When categories share the same literal values, the model may not keep track of which column each value belongs to, leading to cross‑category assignment.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Maintain separate lists for each category and always assign values from the correct list to the corresponding column; resolve ambiguous clues by context.
